$comment: PHASE 12 POINT 3 — registry of every compatibility adapter left standing after the CaseEvidence and Legal-Hold cutovers. An adapter is any module or route that exists ONLY to keep a superseded surface working while its physical contract migration is unapplied. Every entry MUST carry a removal condition naming the exact owner-run migration and the exact verification that discharges it; an adapter without one is 'conditionless' and is a defect, because nobody can ever prove it is safe to delete. ConditionlessAdapters counts entries whose removalCondition is null.

That was wrong: their retention condition is an OWNER-RUN production migration that has not been applied, and zero repository callers is explicitly not sufficient on its own. They were reconstructed from their executable contracts (test/phase-12-trust-administration-residue-matrix.test.ts and test/phase-12-legal-hold-compatibility.test.ts) as thin canonical delegates, and are classified REQUIRED_MIGRATION_COMPATIBILITY below.

separateFindings.finding: resolveWorkspace resolves the caller's current workspace and performs NO authorization: it reads User.currentWorkspaceId and returns it. It never calls authorizeOrFail, so no capability, ACTIVE-membership, parent-Organization-lifecycle or anti-enumeration check runs at that seam.
separateFindings.notInsecureByHelperNameAlone: Route-level proof was taken, not inferred. Membership is implied because currentWorkspaceId is written only by the audited workspace switcher, and 22 of the 44 routes additionally carry requireDelegatedTierAny([ORG_ADMIN, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER]) — that covers the destructive lifecycle operations (destruction approve/reject/execute, chain-transfer accept/complete/revoke, archive transition, retention release, webhook deactivate/replay, entitlement grant). Those are NOT unauthenticated and NOT ungated.
separateFindings.actualGap: No CAPABILITY check runs on the 22 requireAuth-only routes, and the canonical primitive's ACTIVE-membership + Organization-lifecycle + anti-enumeration guarantees run on none of the 40 ungated call sites. Highest-priority for review because they mutate or mint credentials rather than read: POST /v1/exchange/packages, POST /v1/exchange/packages/:id/sign-url, POST /v1/exchange/packages/:id/deliveries, POST /v1/exchange/deliveries/:id/download.
separateFindings.requiredReview: For each of the 40 remaining call sites, determine the canonical permission for its surface and route it through authorizeOrFail, as services/api/src/routes/intelligence-platform.routes.ts already does. Do not assume the delegated-tier preHandler is equivalent: it gates WHO may reach the route, not what they may do in THIS workspace.

passIntakePseudonym.finding: `openIntakeSession` accepted `pseudonym` / `submitterDisplayName` / `submitterEmail`, and the reviewer-side summary projected them, but the only public entry point was GET /v1/external-intake/:token — a request with no body that passed none of them. Every EXTERNAL_PSEUDONYMOUS session therefore persisted a null pseudonym while the workspace UI shipped the mode as 'Display name — contributor chooses a name shown with the submission'.
resolution: `recordIntakeSubmitterIdentity` is now the ONE writer of the three identity columns; `openIntakeSession` no longer accepts them and always persists null (identity must never travel in a URL).

New token-bound mutation POST /v1/external-intake/:token/sessions/:sid/identity, behind the same feature gate and rate limits as every other public intake route. The workspace comes from the persisted link resolved by the validated token, never from the request.

Mode policy is server-side and fail-closed: PSEUDONYMOUS accepts a pseudonym only; ANONYMOUS and every non-external mode accept nothing; ONE_TIME/REUSABLE accept an opt-in display name and/or email. A mismatched field is REFUSED (`intake_mode_mismatch`), not silently dropped.
Contributor text is normalized (control/invisible characters stripped, whitespace collapsed, bounded) and an all-whitespace value is 'not provided' rather than a blank identity.
The public intake page collects the display name for that mode only, blocks continuation until it is entered, and does not proceed to consent if the mutation is refused.
No identity is echoed: the public session projection has no identity field, and the failure message names the requirement rather than the submitted value.

p5ReportGenerationAuthority.guarded: Every statement is IF NOT EXISTS. The table is NEW, so there is no backfill, no data movement and nothing to lose; a failed apply leaves the prior state exactly intact. No existing column is altered or dropped, so a deployment still running the previous build is unaffected until its code is replaced.
p5ReportGenerationAuthority.idempotent: Re-running after a successful apply is a clean no-op — verified by applying twice against a disposable PostgreSQL 16 with the full migration history.
p5ReportGenerationAuthority.whyRequired: Report generation was requested by putting { evidenceId, forceRegenerate, regenerateReason } on a BullMQ payload. `forceRegenerate` is the outcome of an authorization decision — it bypasses the guard refusing to regenerate an already-REPORTED artifact — and it arrived as an unverified boolean on a queue message. The authorized synchronous path now persists the intent in report_generation_requests and the queue carries only that row's id.
p5ReportGenerationAuthority.rehearsal: Applied to disposable PostgreSQL 16 (postgres:16) over the complete migration history; `prisma migrate deploy` reported all migrations applied, and a second run reported no pending migrations.

categories.$comment: PHASE 12 POINT 4 — five explicit categories. `adapters` is the registry of RUNTIME entries; a database migration is never one of them (migrations live in `ownerPending`). Every entry carries `category`, and the counts below are derived from those fields, not asserted separately.

definitions.RUNTIME_COMPATIBILITY_ROUTE: An HTTP route retained only to keep a published URL working while a migration/rollout condition is outstanding.
definitions.RUNTIME_COMPATIBILITY_SERVICE: A service module retained only to keep a superseded internal surface working.
definitions.CANONICAL_RUNTIME: Not an adapter. The current, intended implementation with live callers and no removal condition.
definitions.OWNER_MIGRATION_PENDING: A forward-only schema migration authored here and NOT applied to any deployed environment.
definitions.HISTORICAL_PRESERVE: Data or rows preserved for provenance; never rewritten, never counted as runtime.

ownerPending.$comment: THE unified owner-pending registry for Phase 12 Point 4. Nothing owner-controlled is recorded anywhere else. Entries 1 and 2 are physical schema removals; entry 3 is the runtime compatibility surface whose retention depends on entry 2 plus a rollout observation.
